algebraic_carriers.maps_to_algebra: ring (with explicit overflow: wrapping_add / checked_add / saturating_add / overflowing_add are distinct operations; debug builds panic on overflow, release wraps)
ring (same wrap-on-release / panic-on-debug semantics as i32)
field (approximation; IEEE-754 double-precision, same caveats as Python/C)
monoid (placeholder for product_type; same caveat as C struct - W22 follow-up)
monoid (placeholder for sum_type / coproduct - Rust enums ARE proper tagged unions, the substrate just lacks a sum_type algebra card yet; W22 follow-up)
monoid (under .or() with None as identity - genuine monoid; would also be expressible as 'monoid_with_zero' under .and() but the substrate has no such card yet)
monoid (concatenation via extend / chain with Vec::new() identity)
monoid (concatenation via push_str / + with String::new() identity)

flaws: structure-mixed: 'mixed' is honest but coarse - Rust is mostly nominal with structural escape hatches; a finer-grained taxonomy is a W23+ idea.

sum-type-as-monoid: enum is genuinely a sum type (coproduct in category-of-types) but the substrate has no cards/algebra/sum_type/ card yet. The 'monoid' placeholder is dishonest at the precision level but the only existing algebra ref that lands. W22 follow-up: add sum_type and product_type algebra cards.

Option-not-monoid_with_zero: Option<T> under .and() with Some(_) absorbing-zero behaviour is more precisely a 'monoid with zero' / 'pointed monoid'; the substrate has no such card. We use plain monoid (under .or()) honestly.

memory-model-summary: 'borrow_checked' is the substrate convention; the formal Rust memory model is still under active spec (Stacked Borrows / Tree Borrows / MIRI). This card describes the language as understood circa 2024.
Rust-frontend-heuristic: rust.py is regex-driven, not a proper parser - real syn-crate-style parsing is a W24+ idea. The card describes the LANGUAGE; coverage gaps live in rust.py.
informal_description: Rust is a strongly statically typed systems language with structural algebraic data types (enums for sum types, structs/tuples for product types) layered on top of a nominal struct/enum identity system. Evaluation is eager and strict. Side effects are type-tracked: mutability is explicit (let vs let mut), shared mutable state requires Cell/RefCell/Mutex/RwLock with explicit interior-mutability markers, and IO is not in the type signature but unsafe-only operations (raw pointer deref, FFI calls, untagged-union access) require an `unsafe` block. Memory is neither GC'd nor manually managed: ownership + borrowing + lifetimes provide static guarantees of safe deallocation (RAII via Drop), no use-after-free, and no data races across threads (Send/Sync trait gating). i32/i64 are rings; u32/u64 are commutative rings under wrap; f64 approximates a field; Vec<T> and String are monoids; Option<T> and Result<T,E> form monoids under .or() / .and_then() chaining. Concurrency is exposed three ways: native OS threads (std::thread, Send-bounded), async/await (Future-trait, executor-pluggable - tokio is the default in practice), and channels (std::sync::mpsc, tokio::sync, crossbeam). The transpile frontend at cards/tool/v_transpile/frontends/rust.py uses regex + heuristics (UB5-A push toward ~95% of typical modern Rust) to lift fn/let/struct/enum/impl/trait/match/closure/try-propagate (?) into the substrate IR.
name: rust
notes: Rust's type_system.structure is 'mixed' because the language has BOTH nominal types (a struct/enum is a distinct named type even with identical fields to another) AND structural elements (tuples, function/closure types, trait-object dyn Trait). The 'pure_restricted' side_effect_model is the substrate's name for type-system-tracked-but-not-monadic effects: Rust mutability is explicit, shared state requires Sync, but IO is not lifted into an IO monad the way Haskell does it.
standardization_body: Rust RFC process + Edition system (2015/2018/2021/2024); no ISO standard
